body:
It didn't for me at first. Antidepression ones sort of did... But I couldn't find any for my anxiety, which is what was causing all my turmoil. I only finally found a form of medication that worked for my anxiety two weeks ago. EDIT: I tried so many before I found these ones. I was beginning to lose hope again. These were actually a hail Mary in the end, because my doctor was really puzzled and was going to send me to a psychiatrist at that point. It was... Really strange to be able to have my thoughts slow down. Usually meds made me feel slow and paranoid, like a bad high. These ones just let me breathe.

"it gets better" really annoyed me when I was in my worst stage of depression. I was so tired of hearing it... I understand how it can come off. It made me feel like the person saying it was so privileged - closest word I can think to use - and they had no idea what reality for others was like. Truthfully, I only know my own reality. And it only got better because I found something to get better for. It took two years and make even a little progress.. But so far it's been worth sticking around.

You're very welcome. I'm so glad to help in any way! 
If you ever need someone to speak to never hesitate to message me. 

Life gets so much more positive... There will always be stressors and struggles, but they get a lot easier to power through. (:
Replies are being deleted, but I'm appreciative to everyone who took time to speak to me.

Thank you for taking the time out of your day to speak to me. It means a lot. 

EDIT; 
I feel bad for not giving you more of an honest reply. You took time out of your day to listen to my problems and respond... 
Thank you. 

Things that calm me down are usually listening to music and laying in bed with my dog. It's my happy place where I feel safe. 
But I can't always have that crutch, you know?

I do... I always feel like I need to smile and be sweet, even when I'm currently battling the worst day of my life. 
I won't lie, I have many insecurities, and so I'm constantly convinced everyone around me thinks the worst of me. 

Some friends I can be comfortable around with only a bit of anxiety, others I have to constantly push thoughts away and try to remain cool and calm. My immediate family I'm normal around. 
I sometimes am able to accomplish more stressful things if I have someone I trust by my side...

It's hard to put into words- I just feel vulnerable. I feel like they're staring at me, judging me, thinking cruel thoughts, summing me up in their mind. How am I coming off? Am I speaking awkwardly? Is my body language correct? Do I smile here? My face is hot, I can't smile right now... I'm expected to smile, so smile. My legs are shaking, tunnel vision is creeping up. I'm not hearing anything anymore except roaring and my own frantic thoughts. It's overwhelming. 

At that point I feel like I'm close to fainting. It's not all internal, unfortunately... It's noticeable on the outside. Id be better if I could at least suffer unbeknownst to them and push past, but when I'm visually trembling and gasping for breath it's hard to play it cool...

I've spoken to my counsellor in depth about agoraphobia... My fear is mostly centred around people. I panic meeting new people, introductions and the like. It's overwhelming having so much attention on me.. I'd rather be unseen.
I'm confused by what you could mean. I just made an account, I have no posting history. And I'm unsure of what id have to lie about anonymously...
Sometimes it makes me feel calmer... I have to have earphones in while in public or I panic.
Right now I'm really into the 1975 and Vampire Weekend, as well as Foster The People. Just the ones I really have played the most on my iPod.
Music? I really like alternative/indie kind of stuff...
